title: Actual Bochner means are controlled by the all-coupling quadratic cost
source_anchor: Samplinglib original feature differentiation and transport supplement v1, 2026-10-21; units[3] and its complete formula proof
target_statement: Let U be any measurable space and H a complete real normed vector space. Let K:U→H be strongly measurable with ‖K(u)‖≤B. Let c:U×U→ℝ be measurable with 0≤c(z)≤C, and suppose ‖K(u)−K(v)‖≤L c(u,v), where B,C,L≥0. For any two probability measures μ,ν on U, define Q as the infimum, over all actual couplings π with these two marginals, of ∫c² dπ, interpreted as an extended nonnegative integral; set W=Q^(1/2). Then K is genuinely Bochner integrable under each law, Q is finite, and ‖∫K dμ−∫K dν‖≤L W.toReal. For every y∈H both residual norms are at most B+‖y‖. No optimizer, chosen-plan bound, finite-cost assumption or mean-identity premise is supplied. U need not carry a vector-space structure, and c need not be a metric.
